title: Screening paper 3
intro: Fifty questions in 20 minutes, and a wrong answer costs nothing, so answer every one. Fifteen are accounts, audit and tax, so revise your Inter basics before you sit it and give that section its full 6 minutes.

questions.stem: Choose the word that fills the blank in this formal note: “Mr Bhatia, ___ the partner asked to review the stock sheets, found two errors in them.”
questions.reason: The partner asked him to review the sheets, so the pronoun is the object of ‘asked’: ‘whom’. ‘Who’ is for the one doing the action, ‘whose’ shows ownership, and ‘which’ is not used for a person.

questions.stem: What does ‘expedite’ mean in this sentence? “The client has asked us to expedite the stock reconciliation before its Board meeting.”
questions.reason: To expedite a task is to get it done sooner, which fits a deadline before the Board meeting. ‘Simplify’ and ‘explain’ are near misses; ‘postpone’ is close to the opposite.

questions.stem: Choose the words that fill both blanks: “Every voucher carries ___ unique serial number, and filing a day’s vouchers takes about ___ hour.”
questions.reason: The article follows the sound, not the letter. ‘Unique’ begins with a ‘yoo’ sound, so ‘a unique’; the h of ‘hour’ is silent, so it begins with a vowel sound: ‘an hour’.

questions.stem: Which part of this sentence has an error? “The new checklist / has helped our team / make less mistakes / in this quarter’s GST returns.”
questions.reason: Mistakes can be counted, so the word is ‘fewer’: ‘make fewer mistakes’. ‘Less’ goes with what you can’t count, as in ‘less time’. ‘Helped our team make’ is correct: ‘to’ is optional after ‘help’.

questions.stem: Choose the correctly written sentence.

options.text: Pooja could not open the stock file saved on the shared drive.
Saved on the shared drive, Pooja could not open the stock file.
Pooja, saved on the shared drive, could not open the stock file.
Saved on the shared drive, the opening of the stock file failed for Pooja.

questions.reason: A describing phrase must sit next to what it describes. The file was saved on the drive, not Pooja, so the phrase follows ‘the stock file’. The other three make Pooja, or ‘the opening’, the thing that was saved.

questions.stem:
The first sentence sets the topic of this paragraph. Which of the other four sentences does not belong?
1. The year-end stock count at the main warehouse followed a simple plan.
2. Counting began at 8 am, before any goods were moved.
3. Every rack was counted by two people working separately.
4. Stock is carried in the books at the lower of cost and net realisable value.
5. Where the two counts differed, a supervisor counted that rack again.
questions.reason: The paragraph is about how the count was carried out; sentence 4 is a rule for valuing stock, a different topic. Sentence 5’s ‘the two counts’ points back to sentence 3, so those two belong together.

questions.stem: Choose the words that fill both blanks: “The late delivery did not ___ our closing stock, but the price cut had a large ___ on our margins.”
questions.reason: ‘Affect’ is the verb (to influence) and ‘effect’ the noun (a result). The first blank needs a verb after ‘did not’; the second needs a noun after ‘a large’.

questions.stem: Choose the word or words that fill the blank: “Our year-end file ___ the trial balance, the lead schedules and the working papers.”
questions.reason: ‘Comprise’ already means ‘consist of’, so it takes no ‘of’: the whole comprises its parts. ‘Comprises of’ is the common slip, and the singular ‘file’ needs ‘comprises’, not ‘comprise’.

questions.stem: Read: “Kestrel Tools Pvt Ltd’s profit rose by ₹18 lakh this year. Of that rise, ₹15 lakh is an insurance claim it received for a fire at its old warehouse.” Which conclusion is best supported?

options.text: Its sales must have grown strongly this year.
Without the claim, its profit would have fallen this year.
The insurance claim should not have been counted in profit.
Most of this year’s rise in profit may not come again next year.

questions.reason: A claim for a fire is a one-off receipt, and it is ₹15 lakh of the ₹18 lakh rise, so most of the rise may not recur. Without the claim, profit still rose by ₹3 lakh, and nothing says sales grew or that the claim was wrongly counted.

questions.stem: Narmada Steel Pvt Ltd, a customer of your client Prakruti Mills, has not yet confirmed the balance it owed Prakruti Mills on 31 March 2026. Which subject line is best for your reminder to Narmada Steel?

options.text: Reminder: please confirm your balance with Prakruti Mills as at 31 March 2026

questions.reason: A good subject line says what is needed, for which account and which date, in a neutral tone. ‘Following up’ says nothing, and ‘why no reply?’ and capital letters read as blame or alarm.

questions.stem: Suvarna Ceramics Pvt Ltd budgeted revenue of ₹60 lakh and expenses of ₹45 lakh for 2025–26. Actual revenue came in 10% below budget and actual expenses 4% below budget. By what percentage was the actual profit below the budgeted profit?
questions.reason: Work out both profits in rupees first: the two percentages apply to different amounts, so you can’t subtract them (6%) or add them (14%). 72% is the actual profit as a share of the budgeted profit, not the fall.
questions.working: Budgeted profit = 60 − 45 = ₹15 lakh. Actual revenue = 60 × 0.90 = ₹54 lakh; actual expenses = 45 × 0.96 = ₹43.2 lakh; actual profit = 54 − 43.2 = ₹10.8 lakh. Fall = 15 − 10.8 = ₹4.2 lakh, and 4.2 ÷ 15 × 100 = 28%.

questions.stem: A firm shares its training budget among its Pune, Jaipur and Kochi offices in the ratio 4 : 7 : 9. Kochi gets ₹75,000 more than Pune. What is the total budget?
questions.reason: The ₹75,000 gap is 5 parts, so find one part first. ₹1,95,000 adds up only Pune and Kochi, ₹2,40,000 leaves out Pune, and ₹3,75,000 multiplies the gap by 5 instead of dividing it.

questions.stem: A trader sold a batch of office chairs at a loss of 12%. Had he charged ₹2,250 more, he would have made a profit of 6%. What did the chairs cost him?
questions.reason: The ₹2,250 covers the whole swing from the loss to the profit, 18% of the cost. ₹37,500 uses only 12 − 6 = 6%, and ₹11,000 and ₹13,250 are the two selling prices, not the cost.

questions.stem: A client’s deposit earns 8% a year, compounded every quarter. What is its effective annual rate, the rate that would give the same interest if it were compounded once a year?
questions.reason: Interest earned each quarter itself earns interest for the rest of the year, so the effective rate is above 8%. 8.16% compounds only twice a year, and 8.30% is what monthly compounding would give.
questions.working: Rate a quarter = 8 ÷ 4 = 2%. In a year ₹1 grows to 1.02 × 1.02 × 1.02 × 1.02 = 1.0404 × 1.0404 = 1.0824 (to four places). Effective rate = 8.24%.

questions.stem: At a client’s factory, inlet pipe A can fill an empty water tank in 6 hours and inlet pipe B in 12 hours. A leak can empty the full tank in 8 hours. Both pipes are opened on the empty tank at 9 am, with the leak working, and the leak is fixed at 11 am. At what time is the tank full?
questions.reason: The leak works only for the first 2 hours. Letting it run all along gives 5 pm, leaving it out gives 1 pm, and adding it to the inflow instead of taking it away gives 12 noon.
questions.working: In an hour A fills 1/6, B fills 1/12 and the leak empties 1/8. With the leak: 1/6 + 1/12 − 1/8 = 4/24 + 2/24 − 3/24 = 1/8 of the tank an hour, so by 11 am the tank is 2 × 1/8 = 1/4 full. After the fix: 1/6 + 1/12 = 1/4 an hour, so the other 3/4 takes 3 hours: full at 2 pm.

questions.stem: With the current, a ferry covers 42 km in 3 hours; against it, the ferry covers only 30 km in the same time. How fast does the ferry move in still water?
questions.reason: The speed in still water is the average of the speeds with and against the current. 2 km/h is the current’s own speed, 14 km/h the speed with the current, and 24 km/h forgets to halve the sum.
questions.working: With the current: 42 ÷ 3 = 14 km/h. Against it: 30 ÷ 3 = 10 km/h. Still water = (14 + 10) ÷ 2 = 12 km/h; the current adds 2 km/h one way and takes 2 km/h off the other.

questions.stem: The chart shows a company’s monthly collections from customers. In which month did collections fall the most from the month before?
questions.reason: Compare each month with the one before it. June has the lowest collections but fell only ₹5 lakh, and March had the biggest change of all, but it was a rise.
questions.working: Change from the month before (₹ lakh): February 11 − 16 = −5, March 21 − 11 = +10, April 12 − 21 = −9, May 15 − 12 = +3, June 10 − 15 = −5. The biggest fall is April’s, ₹9 lakh.

questions.stem: A cupboard holds 10 files: 6 of Client P and 4 of Client Q. An article takes out two files at random, one after the other, without putting the first back. What is the probability that she gets one file of each client?
questions.reason: One of each can come in two orders, P then Q or Q then P, so add both. 4/15 counts one order only, and 12/25 puts the first file back before the second draw.

questions.stem: A print shop charges ₹230 for 3 colour prints and 4 black-and-white prints, and ₹70 for 1 of each. What does one colour print cost?
questions.reason: Solve the two equations together. ₹20 is the price of a black-and-white print, ₹35 splits ₹70 equally, and ₹100 is two colour prints, not one.
questions.working: Colour print = c, black-and-white print = b. c + b = 70, so 4c + 4b = 280. Take away 3c + 4b = 230: c = ₹50. Then b = 70 − 50 = ₹20.

questions.stem: What comes next in the series? 6, 9, 15, 24, 36, ?
questions.reason: Each gap is 3 more than the one before, so the next gap is 15. 48 repeats the last gap of 12, and 60 doubles it.

questions.stem:
Statements: No supplier is a customer. Some exporters are suppliers.
Conclusions:
I. Some exporters are not customers.
II. Some customers are not exporters.
Which conclusion follows?
questions.reason: The exporters who are suppliers cannot be customers, so some exporters are not customers: I follows. Every customer could still be an exporter who is not a supplier, so II does not follow.

questions.stem: Lavanya’s name is 27th from the bottom of a merit list of 64 candidates. Counting from the top, what is her position?
questions.reason: Lavanya is counted from both ends, so add 1 after subtracting: 64 − 27 alone gives 37th.

questions.stem: Harsh leaves the client’s warehouse heading east and goes 9 m. He turns left and goes 12 m, then turns left again and goes 4 m. How far is he from the warehouse in a straight line?
questions.reason: Two left turns from east take him north, then west. Net out the east and west parts first, then use the right-angled triangle. 25 m adds every part, 17 m adds 5 and 12, and 15 m forgets the last 4 m.
questions.working: East 9 m, north 12 m, west 4 m. 9 − 4 = 5 m east and 12 m north. Distance = √(5² + 12²) = √169 = 13 m.

questions.stem: At a family wedding, Siddharth introduces Pallavi: “She is the daughter of my mother’s only brother.” How is Pallavi related to Siddharth?
questions.reason: His mother’s only brother is his maternal uncle, and an uncle’s daughter is a cousin. ‘Niece’ would be the daughter of Siddharth’s own brother or sister.

questions.stem: An article visits five clients, Kesar, Lotus, Mayur, Navya and Ojas, one each day from Monday to Friday. Mayur is visited on Thursday. Ojas is visited on the day right after Kesar. Lotus is not visited on Friday. Which of these must be true?
questions.reason: Friday can’t be Mayur (Thursday), Lotus (a clue), Kesar (Ojas must come the next day) or Ojas (Kesar would then need Thursday), so it is Navya. Each of the other three holds in one possible week but not in the other.

questions.stem: A firm’s rule says: “Any purchase above ₹1,00,000 needs three written quotations.” Which of these purchases breaks the rule?

options.text: An air conditioner for ₹1,05,000, with two quotations
A printer for exactly ₹1,00,000, with two quotations
A projector for ₹1,20,000, with three quotations

questions.reason: Only a purchase above ₹1,00,000 needs three quotations, and the air conditioner is above it with only two. The printer, at exactly ₹1,00,000, is not above the limit, so the rule does not apply to it.

questions.stem:
n is a whole number. Is n even?
I. n² + 4 is even.
II. 5n + 1 is odd.
Which statements, if any, are enough to answer the question?

options.text: Statement I alone is enough, but II alone is not
Statement II alone is enough, but I alone is not
Both statements together are enough, but neither alone is
Even both statements together are not enough

questions.reason: If n² + 4 is even, n² is even, so n is even: I settles it. If 5n + 1 is odd, 5n is even, so n is even: II settles it too. Each is enough on its own.

questions.stem: In a code, AUDIT is written ZFWRG. Using the same rule, how is FUND written?
questions.reason: It is not a shift: A moves back one place but U moves back fifteen. Each letter swaps with its partner from the other end of the alphabet (A and Z, B and Y …). ETMC shifts every letter back one place, GVOE forward one, and WMFU writes the answer backwards.
questions.working: A = Z, U = F, D = W, I = R, T = G. So F = U, U = F, N = M, D = W: UFMW.

questions.stem: On 31 March 2026, the debit side of Prakash Hardware’s trial balance totals ₹2,700 more than the credit side. The draft accounts must go out today, and the error has not been found. What is the usual step?

options.text: Credit ₹2,700 to a suspense account until the error is found
Debit ₹2,700 to a suspense account until the error is found
Write off ₹2,700 to the profit and loss account as a loss
Add ₹2,700 to the closing stock so that the two sides agree

questions.reason: The difference goes to a suspense account on the short side, here the credit side, so the trial balance agrees for now; once the error is found and corrected, the account closes. Writing it off or adding it to stock hides the error.

questions.stem: Jhilmil Lamps sold the same models at the same prices this year as last year, yet its gross profit margin fell from 30% to 24%. Which of these could explain the fall?

options.text: Its bank loan carried a higher rate of interest
It sold more lamps than last year
Its supplier charged more for the lamps it bought

questions.reason: Gross profit is sales less the cost of the goods sold, so with prices unchanged the margin falls when the goods cost more. Interest and rent come below gross profit, and selling more at the same price and cost leaves the margin where it was.

questions.stem: Vetri Exports Pvt Ltd follows AS. On 10 February 2026 it sold goods to a US customer for USD 12,000, booking the sale at ₹86 to the dollar. The amount is still due on 31 March 2026, when the rate is ₹84. Under AS 11, at what amount is the receivable shown in the balance sheet?
questions.reason: AS 11 reports foreign-currency monetary items, such as receivables, at the closing rate on the balance sheet date. ₹10,32,000 keeps the rate of the sale date, ₹10,20,000 averages the two rates, and ₹24,000 is only the exchange loss.
questions.working: Closing rate: 12,000 × 84 = ₹10,08,000. Booked at 12,000 × 86 = ₹10,32,000, so the ₹24,000 fall is an exchange loss in the profit and loss statement.

questions.stem: Under AS 26, which of these is an intangible asset of Pavan Couriers Pvt Ltd?

options.text: A five-year licence for route-planning software it bought
The cost of training its new delivery staff
The amounts its customers owe it

questions.reason: An intangible asset is an identifiable non-monetary asset without physical substance that the company controls, like a bought software licence. Vans are physical, amounts owed are monetary, and AS 26 expenses training because a company does not control its staff’s skills.

questions.stem: Amrit Polymers Ltd follows AS and closes its books on 31 March. It had 8,00,000 equity shares on 1 April 2025 and issued 2,40,000 more for cash on 1 January 2026. Under AS 20, how many shares go into the denominator of its basic EPS for 2025–26?
questions.reason: Basic EPS divides by the weighted average number of equity shares outstanding during the year. 10,40,000 is the closing count, 8,00,000 ignores the issue, and 9,80,000 counts the new shares for 9 months instead of 3.
questions.working: The new shares were outstanding from January to March, 3 of 12 months: 2,40,000 × 3/12 = 60,000. Weighted average = 8,00,000 + 60,000 = 8,60,000 shares.

questions.stem: Medha Pharma’s credit sales were about the same in both years, but its receivables turnover ratio fell from 8 times to 5 times. What does this most likely show?

options.text: Its customers are paying faster than before
Its credit sales have risen sharply
It is taking longer to pay its own suppliers
Its customers are taking longer to pay

questions.reason: Receivables turnover is credit sales ÷ average receivables. With sales steady, a lower ratio means larger receivables: customers now take about 73 days to pay instead of 46. What it owes suppliers is a payables ratio, not this one.

questions.stem: Rudra Castings Pvt Ltd made a profit after tax of ₹27 lakh in 2025–26, after interest of ₹12 lakh and tax of ₹9 lakh. What is its interest coverage ratio?
questions.reason: Interest is paid out of earnings before interest and tax (EBIT), so add both back to the profit after tax. 3 times uses profit before tax, 2.25 times profit after tax, and 3.25 times adds back the interest but not the tax.
questions.working: Profit before tax = 27 + 9 = ₹36 lakh. EBIT = 36 + 12 = ₹48 lakh. Interest coverage = EBIT ÷ interest = 48 ÷ 12 = 4 times.

questions.stem: SA 500 asks the auditor for evidence that is ‘sufficient’ and ‘appropriate’. What do the two words mean?

options.text: Sufficient: there is enough of it. Appropriate: it is relevant and reliable.
Sufficient: it is relevant and reliable. Appropriate: there is enough of it.
Sufficient: management has signed it. Appropriate: the auditor has filed it.
Sufficient: there is enough of it. Appropriate: it agrees with what management says.

questions.reason: Sufficiency is the quantity of evidence; appropriateness is its quality, meaning its relevance and reliability. Evidence is not reliable just because it agrees with management.

questions.stem: While vouching payments at Nirmal Engineering Pvt Ltd, you see a payment voucher for ₹1,80,000 signed by the finance manager, who may approve payments up to ₹2,00,000. What does the signature mainly show?

options.text: The goods paid for reached the factory in good condition
The money has reached the supplier’s bank account
The payment was approved by someone allowed to approve it
The payment was recorded in the right accounting period

questions.reason: An approval signature is evidence that the payment was authorised. The goods need the goods receipt note, the payment the bank statement, and the period the dates in the books: other evidence for other questions.

questions.stem: Kavach Foundry Pvt Ltd has made losses for three years and has missed two instalments on its bank loan. Which SA guides the auditor in judging whether it can continue in business for the foreseeable future?
questions.reason: SA 570 deals with going concern: whether the company can keep operating for the foreseeable future. SA 320 covers materiality, SA 550 related parties and SA 580 written representations.

questions.stem: A customer has sued Prism Labs Ltd for a large sum, and the outcome is uncertain. The case is fully and properly disclosed in the notes. The auditor finds the statements fairly presented but thinks users must not miss this note. What should the audit report contain?

options.text: A qualified opinion, because of the court case
An unmodified opinion with an Emphasis of Matter paragraph
An adverse opinion, because the outcome is uncertain
A disclaimer of opinion, because the outcome cannot be known

questions.reason: An Emphasis of Matter paragraph points users to a note on a matter that is properly disclosed and fundamental to their understanding, and it leaves the opinion unchanged. A modified opinion needs a material misstatement or missing evidence, and neither exists here.

questions.stem: A registered supplier in Surat sells goods to a registered buyer in Rajkot, and the goods are delivered in Rajkot. Both cities are in Gujarat. Which GST applies to this sale?
questions.reason: The supplier and the place of supply are in the same State, so this is an intra-State supply: CGST goes to the Centre and SGST to Gujarat. IGST applies when goods move from one State to another.

questions.stem: Hema starts her first job in May 2026. What does the Income-tax Act, 2025 call the twelve months from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027, in which she earns this salary?
questions.reason: From 1 April 2026 the 2025 Act uses one term, the tax year, for the year in which income is earned. Income of 2025–26 and earlier years is still dealt with under the 1961 Act, with its previous year and assessment year: 2025–26 income is assessment year 2026–27.

questions.stem: Banyan Interiors Pvt Ltd owns its office in its own name, signs contracts in its own name, and can sue and be sued in that name, apart from its shareholders. Which feature of a company does this show?
questions.reason: On incorporation a company becomes a legal person separate from its members, so it owns property, makes contracts and goes to court in its own name. Perpetual succession means it carries on when members change; limited liability caps what members can lose.

questions.stem: Orchid Garments Ltd follows AS. It buys fabric worth ₹48 lakh a year, at market prices, from a partnership firm owned by its managing director’s spouse. How does AS 18 treat these purchases?

options.text: Not related party transactions, because the prices are market prices
Related party transactions, to be disclosed in the notes
Reversed, because a company may not buy from a director’s relative
Disclosed only if the prices turn out to be above market prices

questions.reason: A managing director is key management personnel, so a firm owned by the MD’s spouse is a related party. AS 18 asks for the relationship and the transactions to be disclosed whatever the prices, and such purchases are not forbidden in themselves.

questions.stem: Your colleague Nikhil left the client’s office at 1 pm on Friday. He messages you: “Please fill my timesheet for Friday as a full day at the client.” What do you do?

options.text: Tell him you can’t: his timesheet must show the hours he worked
Fill it as a full day, since he will make up the hours next week
Fill in his real hours yourself, without telling him
Fill it as he asks, and tell your senior about it later

questions.reason: A timesheet records who worked when, so only Nikhil can fill his, and only with the truth. Filling it for him, even with the real hours, is signing for someone else.

questions.stem: To show that every cash payment above ₹10,000 was approved, the client’s accountant sends you phone photos of a few pages of the approval register, which is kept in the accounting system. What is your best next step?

options.text: Accept the photos, since they come from the client’s own register
Test the approvals only on the payments that appear in the photos
Record that the approval control failed, since photos are not evidence
Ask for a system report of all such payments and test approvals on it

questions.reason: Photos of a few pages show neither every payment nor that the pages are complete and unchanged. A report from the system covers all such payments, so test on it. Photos can be evidence, but these are too weak to rely on, and nothing shows the control failed.

questions.stem: In the team’s morning call, your senior points out three errors in your bank reconciliation in front of everyone. What is the best response?

options.text: Explain that the client’s data was poor, so the errors were not really yours
Thank her, note the points, fix them and ask how to avoid them
Fix the errors quietly and avoid bringing up the reconciliation again
Ask the manager to move you to a file under a different senior

questions.reason: Feedback on your work, even in front of others, is a chance to learn. Taking the points, fixing them and asking how to avoid them shows you can be trusted with the next file; blaming the data or avoiding the senior helps nobody.

questions.stem: During the audit of Kalpa Agro Pvt Ltd, the client’s junior accountant asks you: “What is your materiality figure? Then I’ll know which differences I needn’t fix.” What do you do?

options.text: Tell him the figure, since materiality is not a secret
Give him a rough range instead of the exact figure
Tell him you’ll pass his question to your senior, and do so
Tell him every difference must be fixed, so the figure doesn’t matter

questions.reason: Who at the client hears about materiality (it may be the Board or audit committee) is the engagement team’s call, not an article’s, and your senior must hear his plan to leave differences unfixed. ‘Every difference must be fixed’ isn’t yours to promise: the auditor asks for corrections, then judges what is left against materiality.

questions.stem: You are put on the audit of Meridian Plastics Ltd and then learn that your cousin is its chief accountant. What do you do first?

options.text: Tell your senior about the relationship before you start
Work on the audit, but stay away from the areas your cousin handles
Say nothing, since you are only an article and don’t sign the report
Ask your cousin not to mention the relationship to anyone at the firm

questions.reason: A relative in a key accounts role at the client can threaten independence, and only the firm can judge how serious it is and what to do. Keeping quiet, or stepping around some areas on your own, leaves the firm unaware.

questions.stem: You ask the client’s purchase manager for the quotations behind a large purchase. She snaps: “Don’t you trust us? We’ve never had an audit problem.” What is the best response?

options.text: Drop the request for now, since she is senior and clearly upset
Warn her that the audit report will be qualified if she refuses
Ask a junior in her team to send you the quotations quietly instead
Stay polite, explain the check is routine and agree a time to see them

questions.reason: Stay calm and say why the evidence is needed: it is routine, not distrust. If the quotations still don’t come, tell your senior. Dropping the request, threatening her or going round her each fails the audit or the relationship.

questions.stem: The total of the client’s salary summary for March counts the Pune office twice: once in a ‘Pune’ subtotal and again employee by employee. What do you do first?

options.text: Leave the Pune staff out of your sample so the error doesn’t matter
Work out the excess, tell your senior and client, and get it corrected
Mention it to the client’s accountant, and keep testing from the current total
Use your own corrected total in your working paper and say nothing

questions.reason: A schedule you rely on must be right, so measure the error, raise it with your senior and the client, and work from a corrected version. A quiet fix in your own file leaves the client’s record wrong; testing from the wrong total, or steering your sample round it, carries the error into your work.
